title: The Letter to the Ephesians
lead: A letter that begins with a single long blessing of God and ends with a call to stand firm against the powers. Its theme is the plan God has carried out in Christ: to bring all things together under him, and to make Jews and Gentiles one new people, the church. Traditionally Paul's, written from prison, it is disputed by many scholars, and the oldest manuscripts leave out the words "in Ephesus" in 1:1.

sections.b: Chapters 1 to 3 tell what God has done: chosen, adopted and redeemed a people in Christ (1:3-14), raised them from death (2:1-10), and made Jews and Gentiles one (2:11-22), a secret now made known through Paul (3:1-13). Each half of that story ends in prayer (1:15-23; 3:14-21). Chapters 4 to 6 tell how to live as that people: in unity and in a new way of life (4:1-5:20), in the household (5:21-6:9), and against the spiritual powers (6:10-20).

sections.h: Who wrote it, and to whom
sections.b: The letter names Paul (1:1; 3:1) and has always been read as his. Many modern scholars think a follower of Paul wrote it after his death, using Colossians as a model; others defend Paul as the author. The words "in Ephesus" are missing from some of the earliest manuscripts, and the letter says nothing of the three years Paul spent in Ephesus. Some therefore think it was a circular letter for several churches of Asia. The book page and the notes at 1:1 and 3:2 give each view.
